text.title: New Dependency Risk Checklist — Worked Example
text.summary: One complete risk record for adding dayjs@1.11.10 to a browser bundle — MIT, zero transitive packages, three maintainers, clean OSV lookup, no install hooks, three alternatives including in-house, pnpm lockfile commit, Renovate routed to the owner — with a note on each non-obvious value, then the crossenv typosquat record as a reviewer would be tempted to write it and what the validator prints.

section.title: Scenario
section.p: The storefront needs date parsing and formatting in four places. swe:alice proposes `dayjs@1.11.10` for the browser bundle; a second engineer proposes `crossenv` for cross-platform environment variables in npm scripts. Both go through the record on 2026-09-10.

example.title: dayjs@1.11.10 accepted
example.note: `licence` is the SPDX id `MIT` read from package.json and matched against the LICENSE file; it is permissive, so no `distribution_model` is required in the decision even though the input records the browser bundle (r-licence-spdx-recorded). `transitive_count` 0 came from a pnpm dry run, not from the README's "zero dependencies" claim (r-transitive-footprint-counted). Three maintainers and a release two months old mean no `fallback` is required (r-maintainer-and-release-recency). The OSV URL is for the exact `dayjs@1.11.10` and dated today; `open_advisories` is empty so `verdict: accept` is allowed (r-advisory-query-in-evidence). `alternative` lists `in-house` (rejected: locale and DST tables), `already-in-tree` (nothing covers parsing) and `date-fns`; `useful_surface_lines` 400 is well over the 20-line default-to-in-house threshold (r-alternative-considered-including-in-house). `package.version` is exact and the lockfile commit is in `evidence[]` (r-exact-version-pinned-in-lockfile). No install scripts, repository matches, no popular near-name (r-install-hooks-and-provenance-reviewed). Renovate alerts go to `swe:alice`, who is the owner, with a 7-day critical and 30-day high window; the record reopens only on a major bump (r-upgrade-owner-and-patch-window).

example.title: crossenv written the tempting way
example.note: What the validator prints: `package.version` `^6.1.1` is a range (r-exact-version-pinned-in-lockfile); `licence` `MIT-ish` is not an SPDX id (r-licence-spdx-recorded); `alternative` has no `in-house` or `already-in-tree` entry (r-alternative-considered-including-in-house); `decision.statement` names no `name@version`; cross-field: `open_advisories` non-empty with `verdict: accept` (r-advisory-query-in-evidence); `maintainers` 1 and `last_release` over 12 months old with no `fallback` (r-maintainer-and-release-recency); `popular_near_name` is `cross-env`, `repository_matches` is false and the postinstall hook posts `process.env` to a remote host, so the only allowed verdict is `reject` (r-install-hooks-and-provenance-reviewed); `alert_routing.recipient` `team:platform` is not the owner (r-upgrade-owner-and-patch-window). What the reviewer sees without the validator: the package name is the 2017 typosquat campaign, one character away from the package everyone meant (fm-typosquat-or-install-hook).
